atoms.text: After Martin Luther King Jr. was murdered, the Civil Rights Movement ended in 1968.
Almost 40 years later, in 2008, the first African-American president was elected. Click the correct time.

atoms.a: Do you know the name of the first African American president?

hint.sound: <lang xml:lang='en-GB'>a beacon of hope</lang> bedeutet ein Hoffnungsträger
hint.label: Info

atoms.b: Barack Hussein Obama II was born in Honolulu, Hawaii, in ((1961)). After studying political science and law at ((Harvard_University)), he was elected to the Illinois Senate in ((1996)) and then to the US Senate in ((2004)). He was soon seen as a beacon of hope for the ((Democratic)) Party — particularly thanks to his highly acclaimed speech at the 2004 party conference. In ((2008)), Obama made history: he was elected the ((44th)) President of the United States — and thus the first African-American President. His election campaign with the slogan ((‘Yes,_we_can’)) mobilised millions, especially young people and minorities. He ran on a promise of hope and change and won against the ((Republican)) John McCain. One of his most significant achievements as president was the passing of the Affordable Care Act — often called Obamacare. His Vice President was ((Joe_Biden)).

atoms.a: Why was Barack Obama's presidency so important?
b: ++He was the first African American President of the United States. His election was a historic moment and gave many people hope for more equality and justice. He inspired many young people to believe in change.
Barack Obama’s presidency was important because he ended all U.S. military operations and closed every American military base around the world.
His presidency was important because he completely changed the U.S. school system and made university free for all students in America.
